standard_prerequisites.name: The first spectral sequence of a complex of functors converges and relates the higher direct images of the terms to those of the complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the local boundedness and quasi-coherence of the pushforward of the complex.

standard_prerequisites.name: Higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules under a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism are quasi-coherent, and the biregular spectral sequence converges
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the quasi-coherence statement needed for parts (1) and (2).

standard_prerequisites.name: The induction principle on quasi-compact opens reduces a statement about all quasi-compact opens to the affine case, and relative Mayer-Vietoris plus the behaviour of tor amplitude in triangles handles the union step
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces part (3) to the affine case, where the pushforward is computed by an acyclic resolution.

standard_prerequisites.name: For an affine morphism the higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules vanish, so the pushforward of the complex is the complex of the pushforwards
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the pushforward in the affine case into a bounded complex of flat modules, giving finite tor dimension.

standard_prerequisites.name: The projection formula supplies a functorial comparison map between the two sides of the base change statements
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces parts (4) and (5) to showing that the comparison map is an isomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: The pushforward of a quasi-coherent module commutes with direct sums, and the derived pullback of a quasi-coherent complex is computed by the tensor product
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof check the commutation with direct sums that the cone argument needs for the single module case.

core_obligations: Reduce parts (1) to (3) to an affine base: they are local on S, and quasi-compactness of the morphism together with local boundedness of the complex makes the complex bounded on the preimage of an affine open (proof lines 5793-5796).

Use the first spectral sequence of the complex of functors together with quasi-coherence of higher direct images and convergence of the biregular spectral sequence to obtain parts (1) and (2) (proof lines 5797-5802).

Prove part (3) by the induction principle on quasi-compact opens: the union step follows from the relative Mayer-Vietoris triangle and the behaviour of tor amplitude in distinguished triangles, reducing to the affine case (proof lines 5803-5815).

In the affine case use Leray acyclicity and the vanishing of higher direct images under an affine morphism to identify the pushforward of the complex with the complex of pushforwards, which is a bounded complex of flat modules because the terms are flat over the base, giving finite tor dimension (proof lines 5816-5824).

For part (5), work with the flat morphism of ringed spaces to the base, use the projection formula for the functorial comparison map, reduce to an affine base, and show that the functor involved commutes with direct sums: first for a complex concentrated in one degree using the quasi-coherence of the terms, then in general by induction on the length of the bounded complex via the displayed distinguished triangle (proof lines 5825-5885).

For part (4), note that tensoring the complex with the inverse image of a quasi-coherent module represents the derived tensor product, and identify the right hand side with the same expression, which gives the statement because the left hand side is computed by the same pushforward (proof lines 5886-5895).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine base and settle local boundedness and quasi-coherence by the spectral sequence (proof lines 5793-5802).
Finite tor dimension by induction on quasi-compact opens, then the affine computation (proof lines 5803-5824).
Base change: comparison map, affine reduction, commutation with direct sums (proof lines 5825-5885).
The quasi-coherent case of the base change formula (proof lines 5886-5895).
